items.title: The principal divisor of an invertible rational function on a proper integral curve has degree zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the degree of a principal divisor on a one-dimensional integral scheme proper over a field: the sum of the residue degrees weighted by the orders of an invertible rational function is zero, equivalently c_* div(f) = 0 (statement lines 2801-2816, tag 02RU). The proof moves the computation to the graph Y of f inside a projective line bundle, reduces it to the pushforward along q : Y -> P^1_K, and must first show that q is finite locally free, which it does by the codimension one finiteness criterion together with the fact that a domain over a discrete valuation ring is torsion free hence flat. The finite-local-freeness argument and the pushforward computation are the substance, so the claim is H2.
